name: Mykonos
tagline: Whitewashed lanes, windmills and the Aegean's party island
summary: Mykonos mixes a maze of white cube houses and blue doors with sandy beaches, sunset bars in Little Venice and famous nightlife. It's also the jumping-off point for Delos, the sacred island where Apollo was said to be born.
seasonNote: June to August is hot, crowded and pricey, with the meltemi wind blowing. May, June and September are nicer. Most of the island closes from November to April.
arrival: Mykonos Airport is 10 minutes from town with flights from Athens and across Europe in summer. Ferries from Piraeus or Rafina take 2.5 to 5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk in town; buses, sea taxis, quad bikes and expensive taxis to the beaches.
foodTip: Kopanisti cheese, louza cured pork, fresh fish and gyros late at night.
buyTip: Local jewellery, linen and Mykonian almond sweets.

connections.note: Fast ferries from Rafina or Piraeus; flights take 40 minutes.

items.name: Little Venice
items.summary: Old sea captains' houses with balconies over the waves, lined with sunset bars.
items.tip: Grab a seat by 7 pm in summer.

items.name: Kato Mili windmills
items.summary: A row of 16th-century windmills on a ridge above Little Venice.
items.tip: Photograph them from Little Venice at sunset.

items.name: Panagia Paraportiani
items.summary: A lumpy, whitewashed church made of five chapels joined together.
items.tip: Visit in the soft morning light.
items.why: The most photographed church in Greece.

items.name: Delos
items.summary: The sacred island of Apollo, covered in temples, mosaics and the Terrace of the Lions.
items.expect: Boats leave from the old port; closed Mondays; no shade.
items.why: One of Greece's great ancient sites.

items.name: Chora lanes
items.summary: A labyrinth of white lanes, blue doors and bougainvillea built to confuse pirates.
items.tip: Wander Matoyianni Street, then the back lanes.

items.name: South coast beaches
items.summary: Sandy bays from family-friendly Ornos to party beaches like Paradise.
items.expect: Sunbeds are expensive in high season.
items.tip: Take a sea taxi from Platis Gialos.

items.name: Ano Mera and Panagia Tourliani
items.summary: The island's inland village, with a 16th-century monastery and a quiet square.

items.name: Kopanisti and louza
items.summary: A spicy, tangy local cheese and cured pork, served as meze.

items.name: Seafront fish taverna
items.summary: Grilled fish, octopus and lobster pasta by the water.
items.expect: Fish is priced per kilo; check first.

items.name: Late-night gyros
items.summary: Pork or chicken gyros wrapped in pita with tzatziki.
items.expect: Open late for the party crowd.
items.why: Cheap fuel in an expensive town.

name: Corfu
tagline: A green Ionian island with Venetian forts
summary: Corfu is lush and green, with olive groves running down to clear bays. Its old town, a World Heritage site, shows centuries of Venetian, French and British rule, with fortresses, arcaded streets and cricket on the town green.
seasonNote: May to June and September to October are warm and less crowded. July and August are busy and hot. Winters are green and rainy.
arrival: Corfu Airport is 10 minutes from town with flights from Athens and across Europe. Ferries come from Igoumenitsa, Italy and Albania.
gettingAround: Green buses for the island, blue buses for town; a rental car is best for beaches.
foodTip: Pastitsada, sofrito, bourdeto fish stew and kumquat liqueur.
buyTip: Kumquat liqueur and sweets, olive-wood crafts and olive oil.
baseArea: Corfu Old Town, or Paleokastritsa for beaches

items.name: Old Fortress
items.summary: A Venetian fortress on a rocky headland with views over the town and sea.

items.name: Old Town and the Liston
items.summary: Arcaded French-style cafés facing the Spianada green, and narrow Venetian lanes behind.

items.name: Achilleion Palace
items.summary: Empress Sisi's palace dedicated to Achilles, with gardens and sea views.
items.expect: Can be busy with cruise groups.

items.name: Paleokastritsa
items.summary: Coves of turquoise water under green cliffs, with a hilltop monastery.
items.expect: Take a boat into the sea caves.

items.name: Mouse Island and Vlacherna
items.summary: A tiny monastery on a causeway and an islet with a chapel, under the airport approach.

items.name: New Fortress
items.summary: A massive Venetian fort with tunnels and views over the old port.
items.why: Fewer crowds than the Old Fortress.

items.name: Mount Pantokrator
items.summary: The island's highest peak, with views to Albania and a monastery on top.
items.tip: Visit Old Perithia village on the way.

items.name: Pastitsada
items.summary: Beef or rooster slow-cooked in spiced tomato sauce over pasta.
items.tip: Try it at a family taverna.

items.name: Sofrito
items.summary: Veal cooked in white wine, garlic and parsley.

items.name: Bourdeto
items.summary: Spicy fish stew with red pepper and onion.

name: Thessaloniki
tagline: Byzantine churches, Roman arches and Greece's best food city
summary: Greece's second city is a lively seaside university town with layers of Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman history, from the Rotunda and Arch of Galerius to World Heritage churches. It's known as the food capital of Greece, with markets, bougatsa and meze bars.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are ideal. Summer is hot. The film festival is in November, and the city is lively all year.
arrival: Makedonia Airport is 30 minutes from the centre by bus. Trains from Athens take about 4.5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; a new metro and buses cover the rest.
foodTip: Bougatsa for breakfast, koulouri bread rings, meze and seafood.
buyTip: Spices and olives from the Kapani and Modiano markets.

connections.note: Intercity trains; flights take about 50 minutes.
Usually with a change at Palaiofarsalos; buses too.

items.name: White Tower
items.summary: An Ottoman tower on the seafront with a city history museum and rooftop view.

items.name: Rotunda and Arch of Galerius
items.summary: A Roman rotunda with Byzantine mosaics, beside a carved triumphal arch.
items.expect: The arch is free to see.
items.tip: Look up at the mosaics in the dome.

items.name: Hagios Demetrios
items.summary: The basilica of the city's patron saint, with a crypt over a Roman bath.

items.name: Ano Poli and the walls
items.summary: The hillside old town of Ottoman houses, Byzantine walls and the Heptapyrgion fortress.
items.expect: Uphill; take a taxi up and walk down.

items.name: Archaeological Museum
items.summary: Macedonian gold, the Derveni krater and Roman finds.

items.name: Waterfront promenade
items.summary: A long seafront walk from Aristotelous Square past the Umbrellas sculpture.
items.tip: Walk to the Umbrellas at sunset.

items.name: Royal Tombs of Vergina
items.summary: The underground museum of Philip II's tomb, with gold and ivory treasures.

items.name: Bougatsa
items.summary: Flaky filo pie filled with custard, cheese or mince, dusted with sugar.
items.tip: Try the cream one with cinnamon.

items.name: Modiano and Kapani markets
items.summary: Covered markets of fish, spices and olives with small meze bars.
items.tip: Have ouzo and meze in the market.

items.name: Koulouri
items.summary: Sesame bread rings sold from street carts.
items.expect: Cheap and fresh in the morning.

name: Meteora
tagline: Monasteries perched on towering rock pillars
summary: Above the town of Kalambaka, giant sandstone pillars rise from the plain, and six monasteries still sit on top, built by monks from the 14th century. Hiking trails and sunset viewpoints make it one of the most spectacular places in Greece.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best for hiking. Summer is hot and busy midday. Each monastery closes one or two days a week, so check before you go.
arrival: Trains from Athens take about 4.5 to 5 hours to Kalambaka, usually changing at Palaiofarsalos. Buses also run via Trikala.
gettingAround: Walk or hike up from Kalambaka or Kastraki, take a local bus, or join a tour.
foodTip: Thessalian pies, spetzofai sausage stew and grilled meats.

connections.note: Usually with a change at Palaiofarsalos.
Usually with a change; buses too.

items.name: Great Meteoron
items.summary: The largest and highest monastery, with a museum, frescoes and old kitchens.
items.expect: Dress modestly; skirts are lent at the door.

items.name: Varlaam Monastery
items.summary: A monastery with fine frescoes and the old rope-and-net winch tower.

items.name: Roussanou Monastery
items.summary: A nunnery built right to the edge of its pillar, reached by a bridge.
items.tip: Photograph it from the road bend.

items.name: Holy Trinity Monastery
items.summary: A monastery on a sheer pillar, reached by 140 steps, seen in a James Bond film.

items.name: St Stephen's Monastery
items.summary: An easy-to-reach nunnery with views over Kalambaka.

items.name: Sunset Rock
items.summary: A rocky lookout with views over the pillars and monasteries at golden hour.

items.name: Monastery hiking trails
items.summary: Old monk paths linking Kastraki and Kalambaka to the monasteries.
items.tip: Join a guided hike for the hermit caves.

items.name: Thessalian pies
items.summary: Spinach, cheese or leek pies with homemade filo.

items.name: Spetzofai
items.summary: Country sausage stewed with peppers and tomato.

items.name: Taverna grill
items.summary: Grilled lamb chops, souvlaki and village salad.

name: Delphi
tagline: The ancient oracle on the slopes of Mount Parnassus
summary: Ancient Greeks believed Delphi was the centre of the world, and came to consult the oracle of Apollo. Its temple, theatre and stadium climb a mountainside above an olive-filled valley, with one of Greece's best museums nearby.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are ideal. Summer middays are hot; go early. Winter brings snow to nearby Parnassus ski slopes.
arrival: Buses from Athens take about 3 hours; many people come on a day tour or by car.
gettingAround: Walk; the village and the site are close together.
foodTip: Formaela cheese, roast lamb and mountain honey.
buyTip: Arachova rugs, honey and local cheese.

connections.note: KTEL buses; about 2.5 hours by car.

items.name: Sanctuary of Apollo
items.summary: The Sacred Way climbs past treasuries to the Temple of Apollo, theatre and stadium.
items.tip: Climb to the stadium for the view.

items.name: Delphi Archaeological Museum
items.summary: The bronze Charioteer, the Sphinx of the Naxians and temple sculptures.
items.tip: Save it for the hot midday.

items.name: Tholos of Athena Pronaia
items.summary: A graceful circular temple below the main site.
items.tip: Walk down from the Castalian Spring.

items.name: Castalian Spring
items.summary: The sacred spring where pilgrims purified themselves.
items.tip: Stop on the way to the Tholos.

items.name: Arachova
items.summary: A mountain village of stone houses, rugs and cafés on Parnassus.

items.name: Hosios Loukas Monastery
items.summary: An 11th-century monastery with golden Byzantine mosaics.
items.tip: Combine with the drive from Athens.

items.name: Galaxidi
items.summary: A pretty harbour town of sea captains' mansions.

items.name: Formaela cheese
items.summary: A chewy local cheese, grilled and served with lemon.

items.name: Roast lamb
items.summary: Slow-roasted lamb with potatoes and herbs.

items.name: Village salad with a view
items.summary: Tomato, cucumber, olives and feta with local olive oil.

name: Nafplio
tagline: Greece's elegant first capital, with Mycenae next door
summary: Nafplio is a seaside town of Venetian mansions, marble squares and bougainvillea, watched over by the Palamidi fortress. It was the first capital of modern Greece, and it's the best base for Mycenae and the theatre of Epidaurus.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are perfect. Summer is hot but the Epidaurus festival brings performances. Athenians visit at weekends.
arrival: Buses from Athens take about 2.5 hours; it's about 2 hours by car.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; buses or a car for Mycenae and Epidaurus.
buyTip: Komboloi worry beads, olive oil and Nemea wine.

connections.note: KTEL buses; about 2 hours by car.

items.name: Palamidi Fortress
items.summary: A Venetian fortress reached by nearly 1,000 steps, with views over the gulf.
items.expect: Hot climb; go early or drive up.

items.name: Bourtzi
items.summary: A small castle on an islet in the harbour.

items.name: Old town and Syntagma Square
items.summary: Marble squares, Venetian buildings and lanes of flowering balconies.
items.tip: Visit the archaeological museum on the square.

items.name: Arvanitia promenade
items.summary: A clifftop walk around the headland to Arvanitia beach.

items.name: Mycenae
items.summary: The citadel of Agamemnon, with the Lion Gate and beehive tombs.
items.tip: See the Treasury of Atreus tomb.

items.name: Theatre of Epidaurus
items.summary: A 4th-century BC theatre with near-perfect acoustics.
items.tip: Drop a coin in the centre and listen from the top.

items.name: Tiryns
items.summary: Mycenaean walls of giant 'cyclopean' stones.

items.name: Harbour fish taverna
items.summary: Grilled sea bream, fried calamari and salads by the water.

items.name: Moussaka
items.summary: Layers of aubergine, spiced mince and béchamel.

items.name: Loukoumades

name: Paros
tagline: Relaxed Cycladic villages, beaches and Antiparos
summary: Paros is the easygoing heart of the Cyclades, with white villages, a famous Byzantine church, the fishing harbour of Naoussa and good beaches for swimming and windsurfing. Ferries make it a hub for island hopping.
seasonNote: June and September are warm and less crowded than July and August. The meltemi wind is strong in summer, great for windsurfing.
arrival: Ferries from Piraeus take 3 to 4.5 hours. Small flights from Athens take 40 minutes.
gettingAround: Island buses, scooters or a rental car.
foodTip: Grilled octopus, gouna sun-dried mackerel and souma spirit.
buyTip: Paros marble crafts and local wine.
baseArea: Parikia for ferries, or Naoussa for charm

items.name: Naoussa
items.summary: A fishing harbour of white houses, octopus drying in the sun and a small Venetian castle.

items.name: Panagia Ekatontapiliani
items.summary: The 'Church of 100 Doors', one of Greece's oldest Byzantine churches.

items.name: Lefkes and the Byzantine path
items.summary: A hill village with marble lanes, and an old stone path down to Prodromos.
items.tip: Walk the path in the morning.

items.name: Kolymbithres beach
items.summary: Smooth granite rocks forming small pools and coves.

items.name: Antiparos and its cave
items.summary: A small island with a laid-back village and a huge stalactite cave.
items.tip: Visit the cave, then lunch in the village.

items.name: Parikia old town and Kastro
items.summary: A Frankish castle wall built of ancient marble, and sunset bars on the seafront.
items.tip: Watch the sunset from the seafront.

items.name: Golden Beach
items.summary: A long sandy beach famous for windsurfing and kitesurfing.

items.name: Grilled octopus
items.summary: Sun-dried octopus grilled over charcoal with olive oil.

items.name: Gyros and souvlaki
items.summary: Quick pita wraps by the port.

items.name: Cycladic salad

items.tip: Try it with local xinomyzithra cheese.
